chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the meal is placed, four thousand angels surround it. So when the servant says, “In the Name of Allah,” the angels say, “May Allah bless you in your meal.” Then they say to the Satan, “Exit, O mischievous one! You have no authority over them.”'
And when they finish and say, “All praise is for Allah,” the angels say, “A people upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, so they have fulfilled the gratitude of their Lord.”'
And if they do not say the Name (of Allah), the angels say to the Satan, “Approach, O mischievous one, so eat with them.”'
So when the meal is raised and they do not mention the Name of Allah upon it, the angels say, “A people upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, so they forgot their Lord, the Majestic and Mighty.”'

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: All praise is for Allah (the closing invocation)
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ: In the Name of Allah (the opening invocation)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of saying Bismillah and Al-Hamdulillah before and after eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the metaphysical reality of dining, where the recitation of 'Bismillah' and 'Al-Hamdulillah' serves as a spiritual mechanism to invite divine blessings and expel Satan, who is depicted as a literal consumer of the meal when the name is omitted. Scholars highlight this as a practical application of the concept of *shukr* (gratitude), linking the physical act of eating to the spiritual state of remembrance (*dhikr*). The narration underscores the continuous presence of angels and Satan in daily life, making the meal a microcosm of the cosmic struggle between divine favor and satanic influence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When the meal is placed, four thousand Angels surround it. So when the servant says, ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, the Angels say: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Bless you in your meal’. Then they are saying to the Satan<sup>la</sup>: ‘Get out, O mischievous one! There is no authority for you<sup>la</sup> over them’.

So when they are free, so they say, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, the Angels say: ‘A people who Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Favoured so they paying their gratitude to their Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.
And when they are not Naming (saying Bismillah), the Angels say to the Satanla: ‘Approach, O mischievous one, so become with them!’

So when they raise their hands and do not mention the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon it, the Angels say: ‘A people whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favoured upon them, so they forgot their Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic and Mighty’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith. ‘

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “When the table is spread four thousand angels surround it and when a servant of Allah says, ‘In the name of Allah’ the angels say, ‘May Allah grant you blessings in your food.’ Then they (angels) say to Satan, ‘Move away, O disobedient, you have no authority over them.’
When they complete eating their food and say, ‘All praise belongs to Allah’ the angels say, ‘They are a people to whom Allah has granted blessings and they have expressed their thanks to their Lord.’
If they do not mention the name of Allah, the angels say to Satan, ‘Come close, O disobedient and eat with them.’

When the table is removed and if they did not mention the name of Allah on it the angels say, ‘They are a people to whom Allah has granted favors but they forgot their Lord, most Majestic, most Glorious.”””
